_about: Night Out's restaurant list (the Where to eat section). Edit freely. area: home (near Needham), boston (Boston, Brookline, Cambridge, Somerville) or north (Up Norf). town is the neighborhood or town; spot is optional, for a square or village. status: loved (our favorites) or try. good: any of Guys night, Date night, Groups, Before a show, Before a game, Outdoor seating, Waterfront, Splurge, Book ahead. site and reserve are optional links. In town groups by town, in the order of areas.boston.towns.

boston.name: In town
boston.blurb: Every corner of Boston, plus Brookline, Cambridge and Somerville

north.name: Up Norf
north.blurb: Up 128, Route 1 and along the North Shore

places.name: Shkodra Byrek
places.note: Byrek, grills and clay-pot dishes from the owners of Elena's Cafes. Big bar, full liquor license, and a curved terrace lined with flowers.

places.name: The James Pub & Provisions
places.note: Needham Center's Irish pub: good pub food, pints, and an easy yes for a guys' night close to home.

places.name: Kings Dining & Entertainment
places.note: Bowling, games and a full menu at Legacy Place. Good for a big group that wants to do something besides sit.

places.name: Thistle & Leek
places.note: Small, seasonal neighborhood restaurant recommended by the Michelin Guide.

places.name: Sycamore
places.note: Newton Centre's grown-up dinner spot, one of the best-reviewed tables around here.

places.name: Buttonwood
places.note: Easygoing neighborhood restaurant and bar a few minutes from home.

places.name: Bar 'Cino
places.note: Pizza, pasta and spritzes at University Station, from Newport Restaurant Group.

places.name: Cafe Mangal
places.note: Small Wellesley Square cafe with Turkish home cooking.

places.name: Farmstead Table
places.note: Seasonal American cooking built around New England farms.

places.name: Krasi
places.note: From the Bar Vlaha and Kaia team: a Back Bay meze and wine bar with a deep all-Greek wine list.

places.name: La Padrona
places.note: Jody Adams' Italian restaurant in the Raffles hotel, an easy walk to the Wilbur and the theater district.

places.name: Select Oyster Bar
places.note: Intimate raw bar with Mediterranean-leaning crudo and a sharp wine list. Recommended by the Michelin Guide.

places.name: Mooncusser
places.note: A nightly four-course seafood tasting menu from Top Chef alum Carl Dooley. Recommended by the Michelin Guide.

places.name: ZURiTO
places.note: Basque-style pintxo bar with a deep Spanish wine list.

places.name: haley.henry
places.note: Snug wine bar with low-intervention bottles and light seafood and snack plates.

places.name: o ya
places.note: A long, expensive omakase in an old firehouse, and a 2026 James Beard semifinalist. The big-occasion sushi dinner.

places.name: Shojo
places.note: Fusion small plates and cocktails in Chinatown, good for a group that shares everything.

places.name: Neptune Oyster
places.note: Tiny raw bar famous for its warm buttered lobster roll. No reservations, so go early before a Garden game.

places.name: Carmelina's
places.note: Red-sauce North End favorite, a short walk from TD Garden.

places.name: Warren Tavern
places.note: A tavern from the 1780s that's still very much open: burgers, chowder and pints, a short walk from the Garden.

places.name: Brewer's Fork
places.note: Creative wood-fired pizzas and a strong beer list.

places.name: Santarpio's
places.note: Old-school Eastie pizza and lamb skewers off the grill, near the airport. On the Globe's 2026 list of the best pizza around.

places.name: Woods Hill Pier 4
places.note: Farm-to-table cooking, much of it from the restaurant's own farm, with harbor views.

places.name: Row 34
places.note: Oysters, crudo and a long craft-beer list in a big, loud room. Easy for a group.

places.name: Fox & the Knife
places.note: Karen Akunowicz's enoteca, a Michelin Bib Gourmand. Handmade pasta is the reason to go.

places.name: Bar Volpe
places.note: Karen Akunowicz's bigger, louder Southern Italian place (she's also behind Fox & the Knife). A Michelin Bib Gourmand.

places.name: Kaia
places.note: Boston Magazine's best new restaurant of 2025, from the Bar Vlaha and Krasi team. A breezy Aegean room with whole fish and a deconstructed lamb-neck gyro.

places.name: Toro
places.note: Ken Oringer and Jamie Bissonnette's tapas bar. Grilled corn, paella, and a loud, fun room.

places.name: Myers + Chang
places.note: Joanne Chang's playful, shareable Chinese, Taiwanese, Thai and Vietnamese plates.

places.name: SRV
places.note: Venetian-style osteria: cicchetti, pastas, risotto, and a patio.

places.name: 311 Omakase
places.note: Ten seats and Boston's first Michelin star. Save it for a big occasion.

places.name: Eastern Standard
places.note: The Kenmore Square brasserie is back, with its steaks, pastas and a famous cocktail list. Right by Fenway.

places.name: Bleacher Bar
places.note: A bar built under the center-field bleachers, with a window onto the field.

places.name: Brassica Kitchen + Cafe
places.note: Bistro cooking with house hot sauces, now in a bigger space with a brick oven for pizza.

places.name: Comfort Kitchen
places.note: A polished, welcoming room built on BIPOC culinary traditions, with a patio. A 2026 James Beard semifinalist.

places.name: Delfino
places.note: Roslindale Village's Italian favorite: big windows, a full room, red sauce done right.

places.name: Lone Star Taco Bar
places.note: Fish tacos, beef birria and margaritas; a brunch favorite.

places.name: Bar Vlaha
places.note: Rustic Vlach cooking over open fire, rare wines from northern Greece, and a room that smells like lamb smoke. Book about a month out.

places.name: Mahaniyom
places.note: A tight Thai drinking-food menu in a lively little bar, with strong cocktails. A Michelin Bib Gourmand.

places.name: Oleana
places.note: Ana Sortun's Turkish and Arabic-inspired classic, with a garden patio in warm weather.

places.name: Puritan & Company
places.note: Seasonal New England cooking with house-cured and smoked fish and meats.

places.name: Pammy's
places.note: Italian-leaning cooking with Asian and African flavors, built around a marble bar. Recommended by the Michelin Guide.

places.name: Giulia
places.note: Handmade pasta, rolled at a big pasta table in the dining room.

places.name: Moëca
places.note: Seafood with a menu that changes constantly, and standout desserts. Recommended by the Michelin Guide.

places.name: Alice & Monarch
places.note: An upstairs taverna for pasta and pizza, with a dessert-and-cocktail speakeasy downstairs.

places.name: Sarma
places.note: Ana Sortun's meze bar (she's also behind Oleana): a long list of small plates made for sharing.

places.name: Celeste
places.note: Lively, social spot for ceviche and pisco or mezcal cocktails.

places.name: Field & Vine
places.note: Farm-sourced, vegetable-led cooking in a calm room with an open kitchen.

places.name: Spoke Wine Bar
places.note: Cozy wine bar with inventive, seasonal small plates.

places.name: Il Ponte
places.note: Chef Beni Kurti's 50-seat Umbrian kitchen on Main Street: wood-fired octopus, house-made pasta and bread, and his own limoncello.

places.name: Kowloon
places.note: The Wong family's Route 1 landmark since 1950: pu pu platters, scorpion bowls, and stand-up comedy in the lounge. There's a plan to redevelop the site, so go while it's there.

places.name: Kelly's Roast Beef
places.note: The Revere Beach original. Get a large roast beef and eat it on the seawall.

places.name: Night Shift Brewing
places.note: A huge taproom with a long tap list, food, and events most nights.

places.name: Il Casale
places.note: Lexington Center Italian from the Delia family.

places.name: Sorella Cucina Toscana
places.note: Opened February 2026 in the old Tuscan Kitchen space, with handmade pasta and a big room.

places.name: Nightshade Noodle Bar
places.note: Downtown Lynn tasting-menu spot recommended by the Michelin Guide. The signature tasting runs 14 courses.

places.name: Settler
places.note: Small Salem restaurant with a Mediterranean-leaning menu.

places.name: Ledger
places.note: Modern New England cooking in a 19th-century bank building.

places.name: Sea Level Oyster Bar
places.note: Raw bar and harbor views on Pickering Wharf.

places.name: Elia Taverna
places.note: A Greek taverna in Marblehead and one of the best-reviewed tables in town.

places.name: The Landing
places.note: Right on Marblehead Harbor, with a deck over the water.

places.name: Daniella's Ristorante
places.note: Reliable Peabody Italian just off Route 1.
